11.stimulus: Psychologists Gregory Bryant, Dorsa Amir, and colleagues investigated cross-cultural perceptions of spontaneous (real) laughter and volitional (fake or forced) laughter. Study participants from 21 societies, including those in Australia and Iran, listened to randomized recordings of 18 spontaneous laughs taken from natural conversations between pairs of women and 18 volitional laughs produced separately by 18 different women in response to an instruction to laugh. Analysis of the participants’ evaluations of the laughs prompted the team to conclude that the ability to distinguish between spontaneous and volitional laughter appears to be universal across cultures.
11.text: Which potential finding from the team’s study, if true, would most directly support the team’s conclusion?

choices.A: The overall rate of correct judgments by participants was 64%, substantially better than chance, and spontaneous and volitional laughs were recognized at similar rates in Australia, Iran, and the other societies in the study.
choices.B: Acoustic features of spontaneous laughter, such as pitch and intensity, have measurable variations both within and across societies.
choices.C: An assessment of the effect of demographic variables on judgments of laughter type in Australia, Iran, and the other societies in the study revealed that participants’ evaluations were correlated with the economic conditions of the societies in which participants live.
choices.D: A variety of people from Australia and Iran evaluated the recordings in the study, and no significant differences in listeners’ judgments of laughter types were found.

12.stimulus: Water flowing around an obstruction creates vortices (swirls) that vary in size with the obstruction’s size and position, and fish sense these vortices to navigate around the obstructions. Using models of three fish-head shapes—narrow (low ratio of width to length), intermediate, and wide (high ratio of width to length)—Yuzo R. Yanagisuru, Otar Akanyeti, and James C. Liao showed that as vortex size increases, pressure fluctuations at the snout increase for narrow-headed fish but remain low for wide-headed fish. A second research team has therefore hypothesized that in low visibility, a fish will be more likely to avoid an obstruction when the associated pressure fluctuations at the fish’s snout are greater.
12.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the second research team’s hypothesis?

choices.A: A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the narrow-headed longnose gar (Lepisosteus osseus) bumped into the obstructions just as often as the wide-headed oyster toadfish (Opsanus tau) did.
choices.B: A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the wide-headed oyster toadfish (Opsanus tau) bumped into obstructions more often than the narrow-headed longnose gar (Lepisosteus osseus) did.
choices.C: A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that some specimens of the narrow-headed longnose gar (Lepisosteus osseus) bumped into the obstructions more often than other specimens of the same fish did.
choices.D: A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the oyster toadfish (Opsanus tau), which has a relatively wide head, bumped into more than half of the obstructions.

choices.B: Greater average Mb levels in a certain species were associated with greater variance in Mb levels among individuals of that species.
choices.C: Less variation in Mb levels was observed among P. buchholzi individuals than among G. petersii and D. rerio individuals.
choices.D: On average, G. petersii had higher Mb levels in their cardiac tissue than D. rerio and P. buchholzi had.

8.stimulus:
Text 1
The land that became Grande Terre island split from remnants of the former supercontinent Gondwana approximately 80 million years ago, carrying Gondwanan biota with it, and experienced periodic submersion until 37 million years ago. Some researchers posit that the island's current biota includes members of Gondwanan clades (i.e., clades predating the split) that persisted by seeking temporary refuge on nearby islands during submergence events.

Text 2
In a recent study, Anna Papadopoulou et al. found that the crown age—the age of the most recent common ancestor of all species in the clade (i.e., the clade's founder)—is 59.9 million years for Grande Terre's clade of leaf beetles. Most of the island's extant biota belong to clades with younger crown ages, however: Igor V. Bartish et al. found that the crown age of Grande Terre's clade of Pycnandra plants is 22.9 million years, for example.
8.text: Taken together, Text 1 and Text 2 best support which statement about the clades of leaf beetles and Pycnandra plants on Grande Terre?

choices.A: The clade of leaf beetles originated before Grande Terre split from Gondwana, whereas the clade of Pycnandra plants originated after the split but before the periodic submergence events began.
choices.B: The clade of leaf beetles must have originated on Gondwana, but the clade of Pycnandra plants may or may not have.
choices.C: Neither the clade of leaf beetles nor the clade of Pycnandra plants originated on Gondwana.
choices.D: Both the clade of leaf beetles and the clade of Pycnandra plants originated elsewhere and colonized Grande Terre.

choices.B: It can definitively undermine that attribution.
choices.C: It can confirm that attribution with a high degree of confidence.

14.stimulus: Northern Michigan's Alcona County is among the most rural counties in the United States: the US Census Bureau classified it as 98.9% rural in 2010. Researchers studying populations of counties like Alcona often struggle to recruit and retain participants. Melissa Valerio and colleagues tested whether a method called snowball sampling could improve recruitment and retention. Working in two rural counties, the researchers identified a small number of people who had the characteristics desired for a proposed study and asked them to recruit additional participants from their social networks. Valerio and colleagues found that participants recruited via snowball sampling showed a much higher retention rate than did people recruited by strangers, suggesting that ______
14.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: people with relatively small social networks are inherently less likely to be recruited to participate in a study via snowball sampling than are people with relatively large social networks.
choices.B: snowball sampling is more likely to improve retention rates among rural participants than among nonrural participants.
choices.C: being recruited to participate in a study by someone with whom one is socially connected may impart a feeling of obligation to persist with participation in the study.
choices.D: social networks can become large enough that two people can share a network but nevertheless regard each other as strangers.

choices.C: be more advantageous for insurers than they are for either current or prospective policyholders.
choices.D: benefit policyholders at the expense of nonpolicyholders seeking to acquire policies.

26.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Broccoli is a vegetable that contains ascorbic acid, an essential nutrient for humans.
• Blueberries are fruits that contain ascorbic acid.
• There is 90 milligrams (mg) of ascorbic acid per every 100 grams (g) of broccoli.
• There is 10 mg of ascorbic acid per every 100 g of blueberries.
• Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, so they must get it from foods, including fruits and vegetables.
• Ascorbic acid is also known as vitamin C.
26.text: The student wants to refute a claim that blueberries are a better source of vitamin C than broccoli is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Broccoli contains vitamin C (also known as ascorbic acid); in fact, there is 90 mg of vitamin C in every 100 g of broccoli.
choices.B: Broccoli contains ascorbic acid (also known as vitamin C), and blueberries do too.
choices.C: Humans cannot make ascorbic acid in their bodies, but they can get it from broccoli and blueberries.
choices.D: With 90 mg of vitamin C per every 100 g, broccoli is actually a better source of vitamin C than blueberries, which contain only 10 mg per every 100 g.

choices.B: Hexachloroethane, a refrigerant, can be used in cooling technologies to absorb heat and release cold air.
choices.C: The hydroolefin ethylene and the perchlorocarbon hexachloroethane are both refrigerants that can be used in cooling technologies like air conditioners.
choices.D: Ethylene, a hydroolefin, is composed of hydrogen and carbon; hexachloroethane, a perchlorocarbon, is composed of chlorine and carbon.
